auditChain.title: Audit chain integrity
auditChain.subtitle: Every audit row carries an HMAC over its own content and the previous row's hash. Editing or deleting a row breaks verification from that point onward.
auditChain.scope_body: The audit log is a single hash chain shared by every organization, so it has no per-tenant view. Only a platform administrator with no organization selected can inspect it.
auditChain.error_body: The audit chain status could not be read. This is itself worth investigating — the endpoint is a read over the audit log.
auditChain.no_dedicated_key_body: The chain is keyed on APP_KEY, which is rotated for cookie and session hygiene. Rotating it would invalidate the entire audit history. Set AUDIT_CHAIN_HMAC_KEY.
auditChain.unhashed_body: {{count}} audit rows carry no hash and cannot be verified. These normally predate the control; a verification run will fail unless they are exempted.
auditChain.head: Current head
auditChain.no_head: No hashed rows yet — the chain starts at genesis.
auditChain.head_behind_checkpoint: The current head is behind the last recorded checkpoint — rows were deleted from the tail.
auditChain.no_checkpoint: No checkpoint recorded yet. Without one, deletion of the most recent rows cannot be detected — run a full verification to establish the first head.
auditChain.verify_help: Walks the whole chain and recomputes every hash. Limited to 5 runs per 5 minutes.
auditChain.verify_scope: Verification is restricted to platform administrators with no organization selected.
auditChain.verify_failed: The verification run could not be started. If this persists it may be the throttle — the endpoint allows 5 runs per 5 minutes.
auditChain.history_help: Each entry is the chain head after a clean verification. A regular cadence here is the evidence that log integrity is monitored.
auditChain.history_empty: No verification has been recorded yet.

anchors.title: Blockchain anchors
anchors.subtitle: Commitments published on-chain, so a record's existence at a point in time can be proven without trusting this system.
anchors.scope_body: The anchor ledger records commitments for the platform as a whole and has no per-organization view.
anchors.error: The blockchain anchor ledger could not be read.
anchors.disabled_body: BLOCKCHAIN_ANCHORING_ENABLED is not set, so the anchoring worker does not run. Hashes are still recorded in the database; nothing is published on-chain. An empty ledger below is expected.
anchors.no_rpc_body: Anchoring is enabled but POLYGON_RPC_URL is unset, so transaction hashes are generated locally and are not on any chain. Explorer links will not resolve.
anchors.empty_disabled: No anchors, because anchoring is switched off.

queues.title: Background queues
queues.subtitle: Per-queue job counts across the whole worker registry. A failed erasure or provisioning job is an obligation that has silently not been met.
queues.scope_body: Background queues are shared infrastructure: one queue carries jobs for every organization, so there is no per-organization view of them.
queues.error: Queue telemetry could not be read. Redis may be down.
queues.unreachable: {{count}} queues could not be reached. The figures below cover the rest.
queues.worker_off: This subsystem is switched off, so nothing drains this queue. A backlog here is expected.
queues.retry_truncated: Requeued {{retried}} jobs on {{queue}}; {{remaining}} still failed. Bulk retry is capped per call — run it again.
queues.no_payload: Job payloads are not shown. Queue data carries recipient addresses and one-time codes across every tenant, so only the failure is returned.
queues.no_failed: No failed jobs on this queue.

anomalies.title: Anomaly detection
anomalies.subtitle: Each finding records the baseline it was scored against and what was actually observed, so a detection can be judged rather than just trusted.
anomalies.update_failed: The anomaly could not be updated.

triage.title: Alert triage
triage.subtitle: Work the queue from the top. Dismissing suppresses one alert; marking a false positive tells the detector it was wrong.
triage.failed: The triage action could not be applied.
triage.empty: Nothing in the queue for this filter.

admin.fapi2Tip: FAPI 2.0 is a hardened security profile for high-value APIs. Only enable it for applications that can meet every requirement.
admin.minimizeConsentTip: Request the fewest scopes your application actually needs — every extra scope widens the consent screen and the blast radius if the token leaks.
admin.rotateSecretTip: Rotate the secret if it may have been exposed. Roll it out to the application before revoking the old one to avoid downtime.
admin.secretExposureWarning: Treat the client secret like a password. Never commit it to source control or expose it in a browser or mobile app.
admin.complianceDesc: Exports are digitally signed and hash-chained, so any later tampering is detectable.
